Add DeepSeek Harness (dsh) adapter; Kooky CLI for non-roster agents

dsh is the 13th agent: `~/.dsh/sessions/**/session.jsonl[.zstd]`, one
directory per session, zstd multi-frame by default. Header line gives the
authoritative id/cwd (the directory name is escaped), subagent sessions are
filtered at file_ref, and the two suffixes are arbitrated in a single place
so list and watcher can't disagree.

Parser notes worth keeping:
- a torn final frame makes the zstd decoder return UnexpectedEof forever,
  so the line loop must stop rather than `continue` — otherwise the scan
  thread spins, ScanFinale never drops and the refresh modal locks the app
- surfaceOp is `'append' | {op:'replace',start,end}`; replace carries the
  compacted/trimmed copy meant for the model, so it is skipped entirely
- usage is per model call, so tokens accumulate instead of last-wins, and
  an empty-content assistant/message exists only to host usage — its
  metadata is read before the empty bubble is skipped

Resume: dsh ships only via npx, and the tui bundle isn't released yet, so
Open In runs `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` in the session's cwd. Kooky's deep
link only accepts agents on its own roster (KOOKY_ROSTER, mirrored from
kooky's supportedAgentIds — Antigravity is deliberately absent there), and
`open kooky://…` exits 0 even when kooky rejects the name, so anything off
that roster goes through `kooky-cli open --cwd … -e …` instead, with the
same CLI resolution and clipboard fallback the terminal path uses.

Add Session locations panel; single-instance adapter roster

Session locations (sidebar footer, next to the relocated refresh button)
lists every path Wake reads — one row per data root with a per-location
session count, click to open in Finder. Counts are attributed by
(agent, root) with component-boundary matching, so codex's archive
directory reports its own number and nested/sibling roots can't
misattribute.

The structural change underneath: create_adapters() now returns the full
13-agent roster unfiltered, constructed once at startup and shared by the
scanner, watcher, refresh, resume and the panel. Roots are a snapshot of
env + filesystem at construction time, so a second roster could resolve
different roots and the UI would describe paths the scanner never reads —
the panel reads the scanner's own instance instead. detect() and
watch_paths() became derived defaults of data_roots() (the single source
of truth for per-agent paths); every adapter's list_session_files
degrades to Ok(empty) on a missing root, which contract tests now pin.
Side effect: agents installed while Wake runs show up after a plain
refresh instead of requiring a relaunch.

CODEX_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME are honored for codex/opencode data roots
(candidate-probe semantics: only adopted when real data exists there,
fixed at construction). Watcher dispatch picks the deepest matching root
so a custom root nested inside another agent's tree can't send events to
the wrong adapter.

Also: sidebar counts render as badges, corner radii are named constants
(RADIUS_BUTTON/KBD/BADGE), tilde_path caches HOME and respects component
boundaries, Finder launches are spawned-and-reaped off the UI thread,
and tests isolate XDG_DATA_HOME/CODEX_HOME (27 wake-core tests).

Simplify Windows support after review

- path_owns generalized to std::path::is_separator with a parent()-based
  bare-root guard — the ownership primitive behind overlap checks, scan
  attribution and per-root counts now speaks Windows paths, not just the
  two display sites (bit-identical on macOS/Linux)

  mod.rs keeps only policy and per-platform wiring, no cfg'd bodies, and
  a new platform can no longer inherit POSIX assumptions silently

  their parameters become one cfg'd call site; Windows launch_shell now
  receives the composed command and reuses it in the PowerShell-dialect
  hosts instead of rebuilding it
- windows.rs: PATH probe walks PATH once total (pending set shrinks as
  bins are found) instead of once per bin; creation flags hoisted to one
  match; shared wide() UTF-16 helper; PS_SESSION const; CREATE_* flags
  from windows-sys (Win32_System_Threading) instead of hand-copied hex

Fix Windows correctness issues found in review

Crashers and dead-on-arrival paths:
- trash on Windows now uses coinit_multithreaded. The default
  apartmentthreaded feature makes CoInitializeEx return
  RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE on gpui's WinRT thread pool (workers are MTA),
  and trash panics rather than returning Err — every "move to Recycle
  Bin" would have panicked across an extern "system" WinRT delegate
- copy_to_clipboard owns a message-only window instead of passing NULL
  to OpenClipboard: with a NULL owner, EmptyClipboard nulls the
  clipboard owner and SetClipboardData is documented to fail, so the
  function could never succeed while still wiping the user's
  clipboard. Also fills the buffer before emptying, and frees the
  HGLOBAL on every failure path
- A failed open_window now reports through show_fatal_alert instead of
  panicking into a stderr that the windows subsystem detached

Silently-wrong execution:
- path_owns keys the bare-prefix shortcut on "root ends in a
  separator" rather than parent().is_none(); UNC share roots have no
  parent but do not end in a separator, so \\nas\agents was claiming
  \\nas\agents-old. Empty roots now own nothing
- compose_command takes the terminal, so ResumeOutcome.command is the
  dialect that actually runs — Command Prompt users no longer get a
  PowerShell string in the success toast and clipboard fallback
- PowerShell cd uses -ErrorAction Stop, matching the POSIX cd && form;
  a bare ; ran the agent in the wrong directory after a failed cd
- cmd lines are prefixed with call so they never start with a quote
  (cmd strips the first and last quote otherwise, mangling paths with
  spaces), and the cmd host refuses input containing % rather than
  letting cmd expand it into a different command
- Add Location validates absoluteness before trimming separators, so
  separator-only input is rejected again
- explorer.exe is spawned by absolute path (CreateProcess searches the
  current directory first) and receives backslash-normalized paths
- probe_clis skips relative PATH entries, matching the POSIX probe

Platform fit:
- Index moves to %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows: a WAL database cannot open
  on a redirected roaming AppData, and the index is rebuildable
- Adapters resolve HOME through one WAKE_HOME-aware seam. dirs ignores
  $HOME on Windows, so the new CI leg's fixture redirection had no
  effect and every adapter read the real user profile
- Theme uses .SystemUIFont, the alias every gpui backend resolves;
  .AppleSystemUIFont sent non-mac platforms down the fallback path
- The delete dialog's path chip uses the theme mono family, not Menlo
- Trash wording, the folder placeholder and terminal availability are
  platform-correct; hosts that embed PowerShell are hidden when no
  PowerShell is present
- Delete-dialog copy is const, not format! inside the per-frame dialog
  builder, and derives from a single noun literal
- Packaging labels the zip from the rustc host triple

Adds path_owns coverage for Windows shapes (Windows-only: is_separator
does not treat backslash as a separator on Unix).

feat: aggregate remote agent sessions over SSH (issue #21)

Stage 1 of remote hosts: mirror agent session data from other machines
into the local index over ssh/rsync, read-only.

- remote.rs: per-agent REMOTE_LAYOUTS whitelist (session data + sidecars
  only, never credentials), parallel rsync into <db>/remotes/<host>/,
  outcome recorded in the new remote_hosts table; exit 23 only counts as
  success when stderr shows nothing but missing-source ENOENT
- adapters/remote.rs: RemoteAdapter decorator wraps each agent's
  with_custom_root instance; keys become {agent}:{host}:{native_id} via
  the new models::session_key single point (strip_key_prefix as inverse)
- scanner/watcher: tombstone queries and survivor promotion are
  host-aware; dedup domain includes the instance host
- codex: state DB rollout_path is remapped onto the owning instance's
  sessions dir, so manual titles and thread keys survive remote caches
  and custom roots
- sqlite_ro: row-cache stamp includes -wal mtime (rsync updates the wal
  without touching the main db)
- UI: Settings → Remote hosts page (add/enable/remove/Sync now), @host
  badges, remote sessions are delete-proof and resume via a copied
  `ssh -t` command through the new ResumeTarget layer

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(cli): ship wake-cli and a Wake skill

MCP covers agents that call tools. This adds the other door: `wake-cli`
answers the same four questions from a shell, so anything that can run a
command — or a person in a terminal — reaches the same session history.

The load-bearing decision is that the CLI writes **no query logic of its
own**. argv is translated into a JSON object and handed to `mcp::tools`;
the text that comes back is printed unchanged. tests/cli.rs asserts the
two surfaces byte for byte, feeding the reference side natural JSON (`5`,
`true`, `["claude"]`) while the CLI sends strings and comma lists — so the
one assertion also pins the leniencies that make the translation safe.

skills/wake/SKILL.md is what makes an agent reach for it unprompted; its
frontmatter description is written as a trigger condition, since that line
is the only part resident in context before the skill loads.

Notable constraints, all recorded in CLAUDE.md:

- Values go in as strings, switches as booleans, absent flags not at all.
  int_arg already accepts strings and silently clamps, so a CLI that
  validated `--limit 999` itself would contradict MCP, which returns 100.
- `ToolError::InvalidParams` exits 2, not 1 as `wake-mcp call` does: there
  the JSON-RPC envelope carries the classification, here the exit code is
  the only channel, and `--sinse 7d` and `--since 7dd` are one mistake.
- Output never goes through println!. Rust ignores SIGPIPE, so
  `wake-cli show K | head` would abort with 101.
- argv is read with args_os: std::env::args panics on non-UTF-8, a
  directory name on Linux is allowed to be non-UTF-8, and
  `--project "$PWD"` is the documented main use.
- The COMMANDS table and tools::definitions() must stay a bijection, and
  a test enforces it rather than a comment.

Also corrects a claim that predates this change: reading a transcript is
independent of the index, but a session mirrored from a remote host comes
from its local mirror and is only as current as the last successful sync.

Skipping the stub files is a separate fix, and the reason a new adapter
alone is not enough: Cursor appends `turn_ended` *after* a turn

  rows, so they are folded into one Meta entry. The boundary is the child's own

  writers that omit it, and an unrecognisable `agent_path` folds nothing rather

  would otherwise attach to the last inherited assistant message now open their
  own host, and the event fallback is truncated without a marker.

  from the copied parent turns, so for structured-source rows only a manual
  rename may override it.

Craft Agents (craft-ai-agents/craft-agents-oss) is a desktop app that runs
other agents' engines: a Claude connection drives the Claude Agent SDK, which
also writes its own transcript into the real ~/.claude, and the other
connections (ChatGPT, Copilot, Google, API keys) drive the Pi SDK. Craft keeps
its own record of every conversation in
`<workspace>/sessions/<id>/session.jsonl`; that record is what Wake now
indexes, as the twentieth agent (issue #44). Checked against real sessions
from a ChatGPT and a Claude Max connection.

- adapter (`adapters/craft.rs`): a header line plus one stored message per
  line; tool rows carry their own input and result and attach to the
  assistant turn that issued them; sub-agent rows stay out of the main line;
  `{{SESSION_PATH}}` is expanded after JSON parsing; a branch folds the
  prefix copied from its parent into one marker (`collapse_inherited`, now
  shared with Codex); hidden edit sessions and task drafts are not listed.
  Native ids are `<workspace config id>/<session dir>`, since session ids are
  only unique within a workspace. The project is the session's working
  directory, else the workspace path recorded in the header, never the
  file's location (for a remote mirror that is the local cache). Sub-tasks
  and branches link to their parent; the link lives in the child's header,
  so the scanner judges it by the child's winning copy
  (`parent_links_in_child`). Custom locations take `.craft-agent`, a folder
  of workspaces or one workspace, and a chosen `sessions/` folder is lifted
  to its workspace. Remote sync mirrors `.craft-agent/workspaces` without
  sources, skills or per-session attachments. No Open In.

  another agent's sessions as copies of its own. Claims live in a
  `claimed_sessions` table, are reconciled at the start of a full scan and,

  written, and are enforced inside the write transactions; a claim is
  released once the original is gone. A snapshot that cannot be read keeps
  the existing claims and links rather than reading as "none".
